articles.title: How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House
articles.summary: Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself.
articles.body:
How close is Donald Trump to Jensen Huang?

The Nvidia boss was one of the few business leaders with direct access to the US president. He had met Trump repeatedly, travelled with him to Britain and, in May, joined him on Air Force One for his trip to China.

Jensen Huang wasn't just another tech billionaire seeking the president's ear. He had become an important voice in one of the biggest arguments inside the administration: how much of America's most advanced technology should be allowed to reach China.

Nvidia makes the chips that power the AI revolution. Washington has restricted exports of its most advanced processors to China since 2022, believing they could help Beijing develop its military and technological capabilities.

But enforcing those restrictions is difficult. Chips can be bought legally by customers in countries such as Singapore and Malaysia and then diverted to China. Chinese companies can also rent access to computing power through data centres outside the country.

Jensen Huang has long argued that the restrictions are counterproductive. They shut Nvidia out of a huge market and encourage Chinese companies to develop their own alternatives. Trump appeared sympathetic to this view, allowing Nvidia to resume sales of certain chips to China last year in return for a share of the revenue, although its most advanced Blackwell chips remain off limits.

But that relationship now looks rather more complicated.

The allegations surrounding Jensen Huang's reported affair with Alice Huang, of no relation but a former executive at Singapore-based company Megaspeed, have raised the possibility that a foreign intelligence operation was targeting not just a powerful businessman, but someone with unusually close access to the American president.

US intelligence reportedly suspects Alice Huang of having links to Chinese intelligence. Beijing has rejected the allegations. Nvidia's board says it has no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised. But the affair has opened up a much bigger question: what did the administration in Washington know, and what did it do about it?

That question leads directly to Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick.

His department was responsible for controlling exports of sensitive American technology. It was also being pressed to act on concerns about Megaspeed, an Nvidia customer suspected of helping divert advanced chips to China.

On Thursday, Megaspeed chief executive, Tan Yong Pong, also known as James Tan, said the company "takes its compliance obligations under US export control laws extremely seriously" and is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". He said the company had co-operated with US Commerce Department inspections.

A highly classified memo was shared with Lutnick about the concerns surrounding Alice Huang and Megaspeed. He resisted taking action against the company, a decision that is now under scrutiny.

Other senior officials wanted a tougher response.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was among those who reportedly questioned why Megaspeed had not been placed on the Commerce Department's blacklist.

On Friday, Bessent pointed the finger at Commerce for not blacklisting the company, telling CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".

"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.

There have also been questions about why an investigation into the Singapore-based company was stopped after Nvidia intervened. The New York Times reported that Nvidia's general counsel contacted Commerce Department investigators probing suspected chip smuggling by Megaspeed invoking a senior Trump appointee. The department allegedly then froze its investigation and handed the case to the Justice Department.

This apparently highlighted a significant disagreement about the direction of Trump's China policy. Huang wanted access to the Chinese market. Other officials were supposedly worried about the national security consequences. Lutnick was caught in the middle.

Ex-Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang summoned to testify before Congress about affair with alleged Chinese spy

Bessent blames Lutnick's Commerce Department for failing to block Megaspeed

Members of Congress from both parties want answers. Democrats have launched an investigation into how the Commerce Department vetted Chinese companies approved to buy AI chips. Republicans are also questioning the administration's approach.

And Jensen Huang's departure has not eased the pressure.

Republican representative John Moolenaar, who chairs the House Select Committee on China, said it was in the national interest for Nvidia and other American AI firms to succeed, but that companies "should never jeopardise our nation's security" by giving Chinese firms access to their most advanced chips.

Senator Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee, said Huang's resignation did not absolve him of responsibility, and urged Lutnick to explain why export control loopholes remain open.

Meanwhile Jensen Huang's team told Republican lawmakers on Wednesday that he plans to cooperate with their request to testify behind closed doors.

The White House has not responded to the BBC's request for comment.

It has, however, told the New York Post that Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick, describing him as "the most transformative commerce secretary in modern history".

That is a fairly emphatic show of support, particularly amid reports that officials are weighing whether Lutnick should be forced out.

There are some obvious questions. If Lutnick had indeed been warned about the risks, why did his department fail to act? And if other senior officials were indeed pressing for action, why did it take so long?

The BBC has contacted the Commerce Department for comment. But there is an even bigger question for Trump.

The president cultivated a close relationship with Huang. He was directly involved in decisions about chip sales to China. And, according to reporting in the New York Times, he was briefed on the intelligence concerns.

This is becoming difficult to dismiss as the misjudgement of one businessman or one government department.

Jensen Huang's personal life may have triggered the crisis, but the questions now reach into the White House itself. How much influence did he have? What did the president know? And who was ultimately responsible for protecting America's most sensitive technology?

Following his example, White House staff are expected to dedicate their time unwaveringly to the working people of the nation,” the memo said, as reported by Politico.The new requirement applies to meetings with registered lobbyists concerning government policy. The Office of Public Liaison will continue to be the primary point of contact for engagement with outside stakeholders, the memo added.The move marks a shift in how the Trump administration engages with Washington’s powerful lobbying industry, with Miller known for his ideological approach and limited interest in relationship-driven lobbying.A dozen Republican lobbyists told Politico that Miller's elevation to the chief of staff position could make it harder for corporate interests and lobbying firms to influence the administration during the final two years of Trump's presidency.“The thing with Stephen is, he’s not someone that a lobbyist goes in and has to crack or try to win over,” Hunter Morgen, a lobbyist at Ballard Partners who worked with Miller during Trump's first administration, told Politico.“He doesn’t operate based on relationships. He operates based on policy outcomes that will advance the president’s agenda,” Morgen added.Miller, who has been closely associated with Trump since 2016, is known for his hardline positions on mass deportations, anti-woke policies and the America First agenda. Before joining Trump's political orbit, he began his career on Capitol Hill in 2009, working for then-Senator Jeff Sessions.His approach contrasts with that of his predecessor, Susie Wiles, who maintained close relationships with Washington lobbyists, business leaders, donors and lawmakers. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Maharashtra minister Chhagan Bhujbal on Friday said there was no concrete decision on the proposed merger of the two NCP factions, with discussions still at a preliminary stage.The remarks came amid speculation about a possible merger between the NCP led by Sunetra Pawar and the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP)."Both NCP factions coming together is a wish shared by many of us, but the question is how it can happen and who should take the initiative," Bhujbal said."There is no final decision yet. articles.title: Ancient tunnels beneath famous Hagia Sophia explored after 3,000 tons of debris cleared
articles.summary: Revealing 1,600-year-old Roman passages beneath Istanbul, archaeologists removed roughly 3,000 tons of debris from Hagia Sophia's underground tunnels recently.
articles.body: Archaeologists have removed roughly 3,000 tons of debris from a centuries-old network of underground tunnels beneath Istanbul's iconic Hagia Sophia — revealing previously inaccessible passages beneath one of the world's most historic religious landmarks. The findings were announced by archaeologist Hasan Fırat Diker at a presentation this fall in Istanbul, as local outlet Türkiye Today reported. The tunnels have been undergoing excavation and clearing work since February 2025, allowing researchers to explore sections that were previously buried beneath mud and debris. NOAH'S ARK SITE YIELDS FIRST LOOK AT CHARRED WOOD FRAGMENTS RECOVERED DEEP BELOW SOIL During the Oct. 16 presentation, Diker said the roughly 1,600-year-old tunnels were built by the Romans and originally functioned as part of the city's water distribution and drainage network, while also providing a protected underground space. Some of the underground structures predate the present-day Hagia Sophia, which was completed in 537 A.D. under Byzantine Emperor Justinian I. Although the underground network has been known for decades, much of it has remained difficult to access, and the ongoing excavation work is allowing researchers to examine previously buried sections of the historic site. Diker's research has shed new light on the intricate network, which he compared to a modern subway system, Türkiye Today said. 'DIG OF THE CENTURY' BENEATH NOTRE DAME REVEALS MYSTERIOUS MARKINGS, ANCIENT SECRETS The tunnels were designed to carry rainwater from surrounding streets into the sea, according to Diker. Researchers have cleared nearly 558 feet of an underground route connected to a fifth-century Roman street, which extends from the Sarayburnu area toward Little Hagia Sophia, Diker said. The landmark, part of a UNESCO World Heritage Site and visited by millions of tourists each year, is actually the third structure built at the site, Diker said. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER He said his team had cleared both the upper and lower sections of an ancient underground burial complex discovered in 1946, excavating an additional five feet beneath it. The burial chambers predate the current Hagia Sophia; they had accumulated large amounts of mud over the centuries, according to Diker. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Looking ahead, Diker said researchers hope to open more sections of Hagia Sophia's underground network to visitors, with plans for an exhibition showcasing the archaeological remains. Hagia Sophia — which means "Holy Wisdom" in Greek — served as a major center of Eastern Christianity for nearly 1,000 years until Ottoman forces conquered then-Constantinople and converted the church into a mosque in 1453. It later became a museum in 1935 before being converted back into a mosque in 2020. Earlier this year, archaeologists uncovered a mysterious 164-foot-long tunnel in Jerusalem near a site linked to the biblical Kingdom of Judah, though its age and purpose remain unknown. articles.title: Microsoft outage hits Yorkshire councils, NHS and police
articles.summary: The issue has meant councils, police services and many NHS services have no access to emails.
articles.body:
Councils, police forces and hospitals across Yorkshire have been affected as part of a global Microsoft outage which has been going on for almost a day.

Tools including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot have all been affected, causing disruption for tens of thousands of people .

City of York Council, Bradford Council, West Yorkshire Police, South Yorkshire Police and York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundations Trust all said they were among the organisations affected.

A spokesperson for NHS England said some local services had moved to using other kinds of IT systems or paper records where possible.

An NHS spokesperson said: "With the global Microsoft issue inevitably having a disruptive impact for staff, local NHS services are enacting long-standing measures to manage IT outages and ensure critical services and appointments can continue for patients today."

York and Scarborough Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundations Trust said it was experiencing some issues with IT systems due to the global Microsoft issue.

A trust spokesperson said: "Patients should continue to attend for appointments and access urgent care services if needed."

However, bosses at hospitals in Leeds, Bradford, Sheffield and Rotherham all reassured patients that appointments were going ahead as planned and that clinical systems had not been affected.

Leeds Mental Wellbeing Service shared on social media that appointments would be going ahead over the phone, and asked anyone wanting to get in touch with the service for support to call or visit their website.

For urgent support, staff urged people to call NHS 111, or charities including the Samaritans on 116 123.

City of York Council, North Yorkshire Council, Bradford Council, Leeds City Council and Sheffield City Council all urged residents to contact them by telephone for any urgent inquiries.

A City of York Council spokesperson said: "Our email systems are being affected by the global Microsoft Outlook outage.

"Our online forms and services are still available. If you need urgent assistance please contact us by telephone."

South Yorkshire Police, North Yorkshire Police and West Yorkshire Police all confirmed they had been affected.

Meanwhile, several courts – including Leeds Magistrates' Court and Sheffield Crown Court - have experienced delays.

A spokesperson for Microsoft said it was seeing "encouraging recovery", but "some users may still experience intermittent issues".

articles.body: A 28-year-old man, who has been working as a software engineer for the last seven years, was denied a B1/B2 visitor's visa as he was planning a two-week vacation in the US, in Seattle and in New York. The man shared his interview experience at the US consulate in Delhi on Reddit, seeking an explanation of what might have gone wrong, as he has a strong profile with a high income and previous international travel history.The man said that he had booked the appointment in June 2026 and after that, he made his solo Euro trip. His DS-160 did not have the details of his Europe trip, but he had included his earlier international travel details, including Thailand, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Japan etc.The Redditor revealed that the interview lasted for 3-4 minutes, during which he was asked all standard questions about his work, his salary, his parents, etc. Then he was told that he was not qualified for the visa.The man revealed that he gave the visa officer all the details of his employment history, his salary of 35 LPA which comes to Rs 2 lakh per month after tax. The visa officer cross-checked whether his income was in Indian rupees or US dollars. But then he was asked one question which he felt decided the outcome of the interview: "Do you have any friends or relatives in US?" he was asked."Yes, I have a friend in Seattle. I'll be staying in her apartment while visiting Seattle and I'll stay in Airbnb while in New York," the Redditor, who is also unmarried, revealed.The Redditor said that any applicant mentioning that they were single and that they had friends or relatives in the US was rejected. He said one woman in front of him got rejected after she mentioned that she would stay with her sister.Redditors said the mention of a female friend could have been treated as a red flag. Many pointed out that even without the mention of the female friend, the techie's profile had weak ties to India, as he was unmarried and living with his parents. articles.body: A 72-year-old restaurant owner in Chandler, Arizona, was struggling to keep his family business running after years of operating it. But an unexpected visit from a stranger and a video shared on social media brought a sudden change. Within days of the video going viral, customers began lining up outside his restaurant, while a fundraiser started to support the business crossed $19,000.Fred Najour has owned Greek's Grill since 2010, Sunny Skyz reported. After 16 years in business, the family-run restaurant had been facing financial difficulties. Like many small business owners, Najour had spent years trying to keep the business going. However, things had become particularly difficult recently.The change began when content creator Robert Schrott visited the restaurant. Schrott makes videos about family-owned businesses, introducing his followers to local restaurants and the people who run them. During his visit, he met Najour and learnt about the difficulties the restaurant was facing.Schrott decided to share the restaurant's story with his social media followers. He posted a video of Greek's Grill on Instagram, hoping to bring attention to the small business. The response was much bigger than the family had expected. The video crossed one million views, and customers soon started arriving in large numbers.The attention also led to a fundraiser for the restaurant. Schrott started the campaign to help the family keep the business running. More than $19,000 had been raised by the time of the latest report, bringing additional support beyond the customers visiting the restaurant.A stranger's video brings an unexpected rushThe response to Schrott's video was visible at the restaurant within days. Customers began lining up outside Greek's Grill, creating a level of activity that the family had not anticipated.For Najour, who had been dealing with financial difficulties, the sudden increase in customers brought an unexpected change. The family had hoped that the video would encourage a few more people to visit. However, its reach turned out to be much larger than they had imagined.The rush was so significant that Najour's son, Nathan, had to call in additional help to manage the work. The restaurant needed more people to handle the growing number of customers and keep things running during the busy period.Anthony Cyrus, Najour's best friend, also stepped in to help. He took on different tasks around the restaurant, including washing dishes, sweeping floors and carrying food to customers' tables.Fundraiser crosses $19,000Schrott's efforts did not end with the video. Along with introducing Greek's Grill to a larger audience, he also started a fundraiser to provide financial support to the restaurant.The campaign had collected more than $18,000 when Sunny Skyz published its report on November 10. The fundraiser was also featured in a November 11 report by 99.7 DJX, which said the amount had crossed $19,000.The plan was to surprise Najour with the money once the fundraiser reached its goal. The campaign was intended to help the restaurant during a difficult period and give the family additional support.Schrott explained that his reason for helping Najour was simple. "I just want to see him happy," he said. "I just want to have him be able to not struggle anymore."His comments reflected the purpose behind the campaign. articles.title: Schools discuss climate change at Dorset Youth COP meeting
articles.summary: School children gather to discuss climate issues to coincide with the COP31 conference in Turkey.
articles.body:
School children are taking part in an event aimed at inspiring climate action, to coincide with the COP31 international climate conference in Turkey.

Hosted at the Kingston Maurwood campus, the first Dorset-wide Youth COP has brought children from 14 schools together to discuss issues including future careers.

Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said young people should be "given a voice" over dealing with climate change.

A Dorset COP 2026 event is also being held on Saturday as world leaders and delegates gather at Antalya in Turkey for the COP31 climate summit.

The Dorset Youth COP event includes discussions about how young people feel about climate change as well as a panel session introducing them to the range of jobs and careers in the climate and energy sectors.

Maria Clarke, of Dorset Local Nature Partnership, said: "Young people are inheriting the climate and ecological emergencies that previous generations have created and need to be given a voice in jointly developing and implementing the solutions to these issues."

"The Youth COP aims to raise awareness, inspire and support them to take action now and into the future."

The main Dorset COP 2026 event takes place on Saturday also at the Kingston Maurward Campus near Dorchester.

The fourth annual event brings together community groups, environmental organisations, experts and political leaders.

The programme will explore how Dorset can respond to climate change, nature loss, food resilience, pollution and other environmental challenges.

The programme will also feature an exhibition of over 30 local organisations and a Question Time-style panel bringing together Dorset MPs, council leaders and independent climate experts.

Giles Watts, chair of Dorset CAN said the event's focus was on making "a lasting positive impact" on climate and nature local areas.

"We want to bring people together, listen to different perspectives and energise local communities and politicians to act more quickly on the pressing challenges we face," he added.

articles.title: A Dallas woman paid $5.99 for a 1930 Gustave Baumann woodcut during a routine Goodwill visit; the signed and numbered print of the Grand Canyon fetched $17,500 at auction
articles.summary: You never know what you might find at a Goodwill store. Sometimes, an ordinary purchase can turn out to be worth a small fortune.
articles.body: You never know what you might find at a Goodwill store. Sometimes, an ordinary purchase can turn out to be worth a small fortune. For one Dallas shopper, a routine stop at a thrift store led to an extraordinary discovery. She paid $5.99 for a woodcut. It turned out to be a 1930 Gustave Baumann print, Bright Angel Trail, which was auctioned at Heritage Auctions for $17,500, including the buyer’s premium, this month.An ordinary trip to GoodwillShe was not looking for art that day. It was a routine stop for the Dallas resident, who was a longtime Goodwill enthusiast. She was out running an ordinary errand and decided to stop by the thrift store. She spotted the woodcut and thought it was impressive. The price tag was less than $6, so she bought it. “What began as an ordinary shopping trip turned into one of the most exciting and unforgettable experiences of my life,” she said, as quoted in a Heritage Auctions press release.She paid $5.99 for the piece and took it home. Its real value only became clear after she began researching it, a process that turned into a bigger project than she had expected.The print was signed and numbered by Baumann. It also bore his distinctive hand-in-heart ink stamp. “The excitement of researching the artwork, uncovering pieces of its history, learning about the artist and watching it go through the auction process has been absolutely fascinating,” the woman said.Born in 1881 in Germany, Baumann became a well-known American printmaker. He worked from his home in Santa Fe and made woodcuts of the landscapes he saw on his trips across the West. The Grand Canyon drew him back again and again. According to the 2019 catalogue raisonné by Gala Chamberlain, Baumann made five colour woodcuts of the canyon, and Bright Angel Trail is among the best known. The trail is one of the most famous routes into the canyon, running down towards the Colorado River, which has carved the landscape over thousands of years.Collectors tend to care about the differences between versions. Baumann often changed a print’s colour scheme from one edition to the next, so two prints from the same block can look quite different. Chamberlain’s catalogue lists this one as number 82, edition II.This print is number 32 in an edition of 125. It is signed, titled and numbered in pencil. Along the lower edge is the artist’s hand-in-heart ink stamp, a mark that helps buyers and experts confirm the authenticity of a Baumann print.The print is in fair to good condition, according to the auction house. However, it does have some issues. The sheet has soft undulations and light buckling along the edges. The central image has moderate toning, and there are scattered spots of foxing, most visible on the back. The upper-right corner has a small loss, and a crease near the top has been masked by the mount. Heritage sold the print as is, and it is framed under glass.You use AI every day. articles.title: Public services in Wales impacted by global Microsoft outage
articles.summary: Schools, GPs and businesses across the globe have been hit with the outage affecting Outlook and Teams.
articles.body:
The Welsh government is among a number of the country's public services that have been impacted by the Microsoft outage.

Schools, GPs and businesses across the globe have been hit by the disruption , which is affecting services including Teams, Outlook and AI software Copilot.

A spokesperson for the Welsh government said they were "monitoring the impact on government services and using contingency arrangements as needed".

Microsoft said it was seeing "encouraging recovery progress" in Europe, but added "some users may still experience intermittent issues". It confirmed the issue was not caused by a cyber-security breach.

The issues started on Thursday, with monitoring website Downdetector seeing problems reported in more than 70 countries.

Emergency services in Wales have been impacted with South Wales Police and Dyfed Powys Police (DPP) experiencing issues with receiving reports on their websites.

DPP also said its general contact centre email address was also impacted. For non-emergencies, they have both asked the public to call 101.

Similarly, North Wales Fire and Rescue Service said it was unable to receive or respond to emails or enquiries submitted through its website.

It assured the public their emergency response service was continuing as normal.

The outage is also affecting access to the NHS, with all health boards saying there may be delays in receiving, accessing and responding to enquiries.

Public Health Wales said it was also experiencing delays in receiving and responding to emails and online enquiries, although screening services were not affected.

A number of businesses and people in Merthyr Tydfil have been impacted by the outage.

Chris Allen, 40, who works at Travel House travel agency, said they could not contact customers or send them their booking confirmations on email.

He said a lot more paper was being used, whereas previously you could "just click a button".

Dafydd Isles, from Harp Funeral Services in the town, said the outage had "caused disruption across many essential services today", including communications with crematoriums and registry offices.

"This has led to delays in some funeral arrangements, with some families unable to attend registry office appointments due to paperwork from the Medical Examiner's Office or Coroner not being able to be emailed," he said, adding that he hoped normal service would be resumed soon".

Councils including Cardiff, Swansea, Newport and Rhondda Cynon Taf (RCT) have also experienced disruption to their emails.

The Welsh Local Government Association (WLGA), which represents and supports councils, said operations "remain under control" and with "no significant impact on services".

A spokesperson said most back-office systems were unaffected and councils said business continuity plans were in place to contact internally and the public where needed.

It added that councils were using websites and social media to let residents know how to contact their services, which is mainly telephone.

"If the outage continues into next week, councils may need to consider further contingency arrangements, but this is not currently expected," it said.

Natural Resources Wales (NRW) also reported its email and online reporting system was down, with enquiries to be made via telephone.

articles.title: Bessent blames Lutnick's department for not banning Nvidia chip sales to China-linked firm
articles.summary: Scott Bessent told CNBC that several government agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".
articles.body:
US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has blamed the Commerce Department, run by Howard Lutnick, for failing to properly oversee the export of high-spec Nvidia chips, as the fallout from the scandal widens.

There is growing pressure on Lutnick across the political spectrum to explain his department's actions.

Jensen Huang was ousted as Nvidia CEO after revelations he had an affair with a businesswoman who was also allegedly a Chinese spy.

Megaspeed, the firm she worked for, had been probed by US government agencies over suspicions it had been smuggling Nvidia chips into China, reports said, but is not on a list of firms that US companies are prevented from working with.

Bessent told CNBC several agencies "were in favour of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months".

"But Commerce has the pen... and you will have to ask them about their internal process," he added.

Bessent's comments come after Lutnick was called to testify before the Senate Banking Committee next month over the Commerce Department's role in allowing Nvidia to export its advanced chips.

Other congressional committees have asked both Lutnick and his department to retain all records relating to Nvidia and Huang.

Bessent said he was "frustrated" by delays in putting the company on the export control list and reports of leakage of AI chips into China.

"President Trump made it very clear that China should not receive any Nvidia chips above H100s, so any leakage is very frustrating because it hurts our great companies in the AI race, because it gives the Chinese an advantage," he said.

Last year, the Commerce Department had been investigating Megaspeed over suspicions it had been smuggling some of Nvidia's advanced AI chips into China, according to the New York Times. Megaspeed has been contacted for comment.

There was also pressure on the Commerce Department to add it to the list, but separate reporting in the Financial Times said the department was delaying efforts to have the cloud computing firm included.

However, Bessent also pointed the finger at Nvidia.

"The story has been thus far of Jensen Huang's personal foibles," he told CNBC's Squawk Box programme .

"The real story here should be: Did Nvidia know their client, and was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?

"It's important that anyone at the company there be held accountable for that."

How a sex scandal at Nvidia is putting pressure on the White House

How AI visionary Jensen Huang was undone by his own bad decisions

Huang has been summoned to testify before the Senate Banking Committee about his affair with the former Megaspeed executive, who is suspected of being a Chinese spy.

The Commerce Secretary has also been summoned to appear before the committee in December.

"Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology," committee chairman, Republican Senator Tim Scott posted on X.

Democrats on key congressional committees have asked the Commerce Department and Lutnick to keep all records relating to decisions to allow Nvidia to sell its advanced AI chips to Chinese companies, including all their communications with or about Nvidia and Jensen Huang.

Ways and Means Committee Ranking Member Richard E. Neal and Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden are starting investigations into the way Nvidia was allowed to sell these chips.

According to Neal and Wyden, Nvidia's advanced H200 chips could be sold to Chinese firms if they were first imported from their manufacturing facility in Taiwan into America for inspection.

A 25% tariff - a levy that is paid to the federal government - was imposed on those chips, under a section of the Trade Act that Neal and Wyden say is meant to allow the US president to take action against imports that risk national security.

"Trump's use of the statute appears to have done the opposite, undermining US national security and putting Americans at risk," they said.

articles.title: At least 24 killed after bus collides with truck near Kaziranga National Park
articles.summary: Several of the deceased are college students, according to local official Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.
articles.body:
At least 24 people have died and 11 others injured after a bus collided with a truck in Assam, north-east India.

The accident happened near Kaziranga National Park, a Unesco World Heritage site, and the injured have been admitted to Jorhat Medical College and Hospital.

Several of the deceased are college students, according to Assam's rural development minister Atul Bora, but they have not yet been publicly identified.

Bora added that witnesses reported one of the vehicles may have been speeding when the crash took place, but "the exact reason will be known after [an investigation]".

Assam chief minister Himanta Biswa Sarma wrote in a post on X that "the scale of this loss has shaken all of us".

He adds: "Our foremost priority now is to make sure the injured receive the best possible medical care without delay."

The bus was carrying passengers from Bokakhat and was headed towards Nagaon.

Bokakhat is best known as the gateway to Kaziranga National Park, famous for its one-horned rhinoceroses.

Nagaon is an important agricultural and commercial centre in central Assam, about 120km (74.5 miles) west of Bokakhat by road.

Lurinjyoti Gogoi, chief of a regional opposition party, said road safety has long been a major concern in the state.

"The government must take it up seriously," he said.

Road accidents are responsible for thousands of deaths in India every year.

In 2023, 172,000 people lost their lives on Indian roads, or 474 a day – roughly one every three minutes.

The count increased to 183,382 deaths in 2025.

Experts say the crisis is rooted not just in infrastructure but in human behaviour, enforcement gaps and systemic neglect.

articles.title: Karen Henthorn 'thrilled' with Dinnerladies stage tour
articles.summary: The ex-EastEnders and Coronation Street star says Victoria Wood's writing is "beautiful".
articles.body:
Former EastEnders and Coronation Street actress Karen Henthorn has said she is "thrilled and shocked" to be starring in a UK stage tour of Dinnerladies.

Henthorn will play Dolly Bellfield in the theatre adaptation of the classic BBC sitcom, alongside stars including Sue Cleaver and Les Dennis.

The show is the first to be commissioned by the Victoria Wood Estate since the comedian's death in 2016, aged 62.

Henthorn described Wood's writing as "genius", adding: "Warm, full-hearted, joyous. It's northern, gentle, it's beautiful."

Dolly Bellfield, the sharp-tongued, gossiping canteen worker, was originally portrayed by Coronation Street actress Thelma Barlow in the television series.

Henthorn told BBC Radio Lancashire the part was "so far removed from the roles I usually play", adding: "I can't wait to start. I'm very excited to explore her.

"She's quite unassuming and tart-tongued, she shreds her friends and her work associates to pieces and every line is a punchline. Every line is a diamond.

"She has the funniest, the most beautiful lines."

Henthorn, from Oldham, stars alongside Sue Cleaver as Jean, Les Dennis as Stan, and Amy Drake as Bren in the stage adaptation.

She said she expected the show to "go down a storm" with audiences and be as popular as the TV series was in the 1990s.

"The characters are so robust, and layered, and so funny. It's not action-packed - it's about character and comedy and relationships," she said.

The tour opens at the Churchill Theatre in Bromley on 22 January, before touring major UK theatres through August, including Blackpool's Opera House & Winter Gardens from 31 March to 3 April.

Henthorn said it would be a "brutal tour" and she would be "crazy busy", with "no time to unpack your smalls", but she would get her head down and "have a fantastic time on stage".

articles.title: Jilly Cooper memorial bench unveiled at Cheltenham Racecourse
articles.summary: Friends and family gather to celebrate the unveiling of a bench in memory of the late author.
articles.body:
A memorial bench has been unveiled in honour of the "joy bomb" late author Dame Jilly Cooper at her favourite racecourse.

Friends and family gathered at the Cheltenham Racecourse event filled with champagne and sunshine for the writer who lived in nearby Bisley and loved horse racing.

Dame Jilly died on 5 October last year , following a fall, aged 88. Her agent Felicity Blunt said the racecourse was like her church where she loved the people, the jockeys, the trainers and the fans.

Racecourse CEO Guy Lavender said they had also renamed one of the site's bars to 'The Rutshire Arms' as a nod to Dame Jilly's book Rivals.

articles.title: Delhi's air turns 'hazardous' as AQI hits 494; 16 stations record severe pollution, 50% workforce told to work from home
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: With air pollution worsening across the national capital, Delhi Environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa has directed 50% of the workforce in
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With air pollution worsening across the national capital, Delhi Environment minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa has directed 50% of the workforce in his departments to work from home, while Transport minister Pankaj Singh has also issued similar instructions to departments under his charge, official sources said on Friday.The move follows the implementation of Stage III of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), under which the Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) has asked the Delhi government and other National Capital Region (NCR) state governments to consider allowing public, municipal and private offices to function with 50% staff strength, with the remaining employees working from home.Stage III of GRAP is invoked when the Air Quality Index (AQI) enters the severe category, ranging from 401 to 450 under the specified action plan."Going by CAQM guidelines on air quality, heads of departments are free to take decisions regarding allowing work from home. Essential services will not be covered in this," a government official said.Pankaj Singh has directed departments including health and family welfare and information technology to adopt the work-from-home arrangement. Apart from the environment portfolio, Sirsa is also in charge of food and civil supplies, industries, and forest and wildlife.The Centre may also allow its employees to work from home, according to the revised GRAP schedule. AQI touches 494 amid thick smogOn Friday morning, Delhi witnessed a sharp deterioration in air quality with the real-time AQI touching 494 at 7.31 am, placing it in the severe category. Dense smog and pollution covered large parts of the city, reducing visibility and raising concerns over respiratory health.According to the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB), IIT Delhi recorded an AQI of 488, followed by ITO at 455, Anand Vihar at 419, Rohini at 413 and Rajokri Border at 402. All these locations fell in the severe category.Several other areas recorded very poor air quality. R K Puram reported an AQI of 391, followed by Mandir Marg at 378, Dwarka Expressway at 369, Uttam Nagar at 363 and Lodhi Road at 341.The area around Dhaula Kuan recorded an AQI of 161, placing it in the moderate category, according to CPCB data.The city's air quality had entered the severe category for the first time this season earlier in the morning. The instantaneous AQI reached 403 at 6.05 am and remained at the same level at 8 am and 9 am, according to the CPCB's Sameer app.At 8 am, 33 of the 58 monitoring stations reporting data recorded severe air quality, while 24 were in the very poor category and one in the moderate category.IIT Delhi recorded the highest AQI at 488, followed by Chandni Chowk at 479 and North Campus of Delhi University at 478. Burari Crossing reported an AQI of 456, while ITO and Jawaharlal Nehru University recorded 451 each.By 4 pm, Delhi's overall AQI had settled at 373, placing it in the very poor category. Of the 59 monitoring stations that recorded data, 16 reported severe air quality, while all but one of the remaining stations were in the very poor category. Delhi Cantonment was the only station to record moderate air quality.IIT Delhi recorded the highest AQI at 452, followed by North Campus at 446. Narela and Pusa reported an AQI of 437 each, while Punjabi Bagh recorded 431.A thick layer of grey smog hung over the capital throughout the day, obscuring buildings and the skyline. The haze was particularly dense during the morning, when several areas experienced reduced visibility. The sun appeared faint behind the blanket of pollution.Unfavourable weather conditions and weak winds during the morning hours contributed to the accumulation of pollutants close to the ground. Several residents also took to social media to report breathing difficulties, throat irritation, persistent coughing, chest discomfort and breathlessness. Some said they were experiencing respiratory discomfort even indoors.Vehicles emerge as biggest source of pollutionTransport emerged as the largest contributor to Delhi's PM2.5 pollution, according to real-time source-apportionment data from the Air Quality Early Warning System and the Integrated Decision Support System (DSS).Vehicles accounted for 31.5% of PM2.5 emissions, followed by secondary organic aerosols at 24.7%.Domestic solid biofuel and dung-cake burning, along with biomass and stubble burning, together contributed 20.8%, while secondary inorganic aerosols accounted for 12.7%.Other sources included waste burning at 5.6%, firecrackers at 2.2%, industrial emissions at 1.8% and mineral dust and ash at 0.6%.Children particularly vulnerable to pollution exposureDoctors have warned that children are particularly susceptible to the effects of air pollution because their lungs, airways and immune systems are still developing.Dr Nikhil Rajvanshi, consultant paediatric pulmonologist, allergy and sleep specialist at Rainbow Children's Hospital, Delhi, said children breathe faster than adults and therefore inhale a greater quantity of pollutants relative to their body weight.Exposure to PM2.5, nitrogen dioxide and other harmful gases can irritate their respiratory tract and trigger coughing, wheezing and breathlessness, he said.Prolonged exposure to polluted air can affect lung development, reduce lung function, worsen asthma and increase the risk of respiratory infections. Emerging evidence also points to possible effects on cardiovascular health and cognitive development, Rajvanshi added.He advised parents to look out for symptoms such as persistent coughing, wheezing, unusual fatigue and breathlessness.Limiting outdoor activities during periods of high pollution, avoiding traffic-heavy areas, maintaining good indoor air quality and following prescribed asthma treatment plans can help reduce children's exposure, he said.Air quality likely to remain very poorWeather experts attributed the improvement in Delhi's air quality by Friday evening to changing meteorological conditions and an increase in wind speed during the afternoon.However, the Air Quality Early Warning System has forecast that the city's AQI is likely to remain in the very poor category from Saturday until November 16. The outlook for the following six days also indicates very poor air quality.The ventilation index is expected to remain below 6,000 square metres per second, while average wind speed is likely to stay below 10 kilometres per hour. These conditions are unfavourable for the dispersion of pollutants, according to the forecast.The CPCB classifies an AQI of zero to 50 as good, 51 to 100 as satisfactory, 101 to 200 as moderate, 201 to 300 as poor, 301 to 400 as very poor and 401 to 500 as severe.Temperatures remain above normalDespite the pollution and smog, Delhi recorded temperatures above the seasonal average on Friday.According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the maximum temperature settled at 31.4 degrees Celsius, 2.9 notches above normal, while the minimum was 16.2 degrees Celsius, 2.7 notches above normal.Palam recorded a maximum temperature of 28.5 degrees Celsius, 0.1 degrees above normal, and a minimum of 16.1 degrees Celsius, 1.9 degrees above normal.At Lodhi Road, the maximum temperature was 30.8 degrees Celsius, 2.8 notches above normal, while the minimum settled at 17.2 degrees Celsius, 5.2 notches above normal.The Ridge recorded a maximum of 30 degrees Celsius, 2.4 notches above normal, and a minimum of 17.2 degrees Celsius, 1.8 notches above normal.Ayanagar registered a maximum temperature of 31 degrees Celsius, 2.9 notches above normal, while the minimum temperature stood at 16.3 degrees Celsius, 1.8 notches above normal.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.title: Man jailed for grooming 70 girls on Snapchat, Wink and Roblox
articles.summary: Bilal Kazi targeted his victims - aged between 10 and 17 - using Snapchat, Wink and Roblox.
articles.body:
A man who groomed at least 70 girls and manipulated them into sending sexually explicit videos and images of themselves has been sentenced to 30 years in prison.

Bilal Kazi, 27, targeted his victims - aged between 10 and 17 - using apps including Snapchat, Wink and Roblox between August 2021 and August 2025.

Kazi, a student from India who was studying at the University of Chester, posed as a 14-year-old white British teenage boy and made his victims believe they were in a relationship with him.

He was jailed after pleading guilty to 37 charges including making indecent images, blackmail and inciting a child to engage in sexual activity.

Warning: This article contains distressing information

Kazi must serve a minimum of 20 years in prison before being eligible for parole and will be on the sex offenders register for life.

Once eligible for parole he will be on licence for eight years.

In a personal impact statement read out at Chester Crown Court earlier, one victim said she had struggled with anxiety as Kazi, who later moved to Birmingham, had "taken away a sense of privacy and security".

"I am doing my best to move forward but the effects are still with me," she said.

"The harm caused is not limited to the time events took place - they continue to affect my daily life."

The court heard that some of the victims had attempted suicide, struggled with anxiety and developed eating disorders.

One victim, who was 13 years old when Kazi first contacted her, said he took her "innocence away".

"I hope one day I can get on with my life," she said.

The court heard how Kazi often used the fake name of "Reece" and provided a false photograph of a boy - who has not been identified - to aid his deception.

He would then demand they sent him progressively more intimate content.

The court heard if any of the victims were reluctant to send images he would tell them it was "what people do when they love each other".

If the victims refused, he would then threaten to "leak" the images that had already been sent to him or recorded by himself covertly on Snapchat to their friends and family.

In some cases, Kazi hacked into victims' social media accounts, shared the content with their friends and published the pictures on social media.

In one exchange, a victim said she felt "uncomfortable" sharing explicit photographs of herself, adding: "I don't want to do it again."

Kazi replied: "That's fine w me" - before revealing to the victim that he had a secret "back up" of images she had already sent him.

In another exchange with a victim over Snapchat, Kazi posed as "Reece" to ask for photographs of a victim in her underwear.

Kazi then sent a follow-up message asking the victim to share her live location with him on the app.

The investigation into Kazi's crimes began after a victim came forward to Derbyshire Police in December 2021.

The victim explained that she started speaking to Kazi on Snapchat when she was 13, believing him to be the same age.

In May 2022, the investigation was passed to Cheshire Constabulary, which said 180 possible victims had been identified in the initial investigation.

Kazi had left Chester - and the university - but was later arrested at Heathrow Airport when he was re-entering the country on 21 July 2023.

He was subsequently charged with 39 offences and pleaded guilty in July 2026 to 37 of the charges, with two left to lie on file.

He has also been charged by West Midlands Police with a further eight offences committed while on police bail for the Cheshire investigation.

Cheshire Police said these offences were considered as part of his overall sentence.

Judge Stephen Everett said Kazi was a sexual predator who took advantage of "what appears to be a lack of proper security on social media sites".

"It is incomprehensible to me why any person would do what you did to those little girls," the court heard.

"This was bad enough, but when one learns of all the other images you demanded for your deviant sexual desires, we will never know how many victims there were.

"Children who believed they were safe in their own homes - and by your gross misuse of social media - you took away all of that safety, all of that comfort."

The judge said it was difficult to find any mitigating factors and said he doubted Kazi's remorse.

"You are a very dangerous person," he said.

"In a sophisticated way, you got into the minds of young people and got them to do things that were totally alien to them."

Talking about one victim, Everett said: "She won't look back on her childhood with any great pleasure - she will look on it totally blighted at what this fiend did to her."

He added: "These are not just pictures on a computer these are young lives that have been blighted."

Det Con Georgia Hughes, from Cheshire Police, said Kazi had not shown any remorse.

"The girls targeted by Kazi were young and vulnerable," she said.

"For many, their interactions with him were their first experience of what they believed to be a romantic relationship.

"Exploiting that trust, Kazi manipulated them into believing that his behaviour was normal.

"Many lived in constant fear of what he would do if they failed to comply with his demands, and some have carried that fear with them for years.

"What should have been important formative years have instead been overshadowed by the trauma of Kazi's abuse."

Speaking on online safety, Sgt Ross Peel said the force's message to parents was to "speak to your children and take an interest in the apps and platforms they are using".

"The potential for online offending is vast," he said.

"And offenders can target children from anywhere in the world.

"By educating yourselves and your children about online safety and the risks associated with communicating with people they do not know online, you can help protect them."

articles.title: Medical helicopter carrying 3 crew members crashes in Oklahoma; one injured
articles.summary: A medical helicopter carrying three crew members crashed in southwestern Oklahoma early Friday morning, leaving one person injured, officials said.
articles.body: A medical helicopter carrying three crew members crashed in southwestern Oklahoma early Friday morning, leaving one person injured, officials said. The crash occurred north of the town of Lone Wolf in Kiowa County, with state and federal agencies launching an investigation into the incident.According to a New York Post report, the helicopter crashed around 3:30 am, approximately one mile north of Lone Wolf and west of Boundary Road. The Kiowa County Sheriff's Office confirmed the incident in a statement, saying the aircraft had three crew members on board and was returning to Childress, Texas, at the time of the crash.“The Kiowa County Sheriff's Office can confirm that there was a medical helicopter crash north of Lone Wolf early this morning. State and Federal agencies are currently on the scene,” the sheriff's office said.It added that only one of the three crew members sustained injuries at the crash site. The injured person was taken to a hospital for treatment. The condition of the crew member was not immediately known.The helicopter was owned by a medical company based in Childress, Texas. However, officials have not disclosed which hospital the aircraft had been returning from before the crash.State, federal agencies investigate crashThe Oklahoma Highway Patrol has taken over the crash site, while investigators from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) are expected to examine the incident.Several local agencies, including the Kiowa County Emergency Management, Hobart Police Department, Lone Wolf Fire Department, Hobart Fire Department and Sinor EMS, also responded to the crash.The cause of the crash has not yet been determined.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trimbakeshwar temple to offer free online darshan slot bookings
articles.summary: Trimbakeshwar temple to launch free online darshan slot booking within 30 days, capping Dharma Darshan at 15,000 daily; kiosk for offline bookings too.
articles.body: Nashik: Devotees from across the country will soon be able to book free darshan slots at the Trimbakeshwar temple, one of the twelve Jyotirlingas, without paying any fee.The Trimbakeshwar Trust has conducted a pilot project under its Dharma Darshan initiative, allowing devotees to reserve slots at no cost and avoid long queues.“The temple attracts pilgrims from across the country. As it is controlled by the Archaeological Survey of India, its structure can hardly be altered and can accommodate at most 20,000 pilgrims daily during its 14-hour opening hours. Managing such large crowds is challenging and often leads to friction between pilgrims and security personnel, resulting in commotion and allegations,” Purushottam Kadlag, one of the trustees of the Trimbakeshwar temple, said.He added that after successful trials, the temple will soon launch the online Dharma Darshan booking system so travelling pilgrims can book assured darshan slots without spending any money.The temple has limited passes of Rs 200 and Rs 2,500 for paid and VIP darshan as part of fundraising, with every rupee spent on pilgrim welfare and accounted for. “While the common man coming to the temple is currently left at the mercy of time, the new system allows them to easily book slots and peacefully worship God,” Kadlag said.Upon activation in the next 30 days, pilgrims can book slots by visiting the website where the Dharma Darshan tag will be available soon.Kadlag said a month-long trial about two months earlier had generated an average of about 4,000 bookings daily. “Of the 20,000 possible darshans each day, Dharma Darshan bookings will be capped at 15,000, including 10,000 online bookings and 5,000 reserved for people unable to use the system,” he added.Executive officer Sameer Vaidya said they will soon run the system live on the website, which is about to be relaunched. articles.title: FIR sought against Kangana over social media post concerning Gandhi family
articles.summary: Shimla resident seeks FIR against BJP MP Kangana Ranaut over social media post on Gandhi family deaths; complaint cites BNS Sections 196, 353, seeks probe.
articles.body: Shimla: A Shimla resident has lodged a complaint with Himachal Pradesh DGP Ashok Tewari seeking registration of an FIR and a time-bound investigation against the BJP MP from Mandi, Kangana Ranaut, for her social media posts, which allegedly contain grave insinuations concerning the deaths of former Prime Ministers Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, and Congress leader Sanjay Gandhi, besides portraying Sonia Gandhi as a mysterious foreign national.In his complaint, Capt Atul Sharma (retd) objected to a social media post published on Kangana’s verified account—@KanganaTeam—on Nov 10. The complainant alleged that the post juxtaposed the deaths of the three Gandhi family members with Sonia Gandhi’s subsequent political rise, using expressions such as “how convenient”.He claimed that the narrative could create misleading impressions of suspicious connections between the deaths and political succession. The complainant stated his complaint was not aimed at curbing freedom of expression or legitimate political criticism, but sought scrutiny of potentially inflammatory and unsubstantiated imputations capable of disturbing public tranquillity and constituting offences.Capt Sharma urged the police to examine the posts under Sections 196 (promoting enmity between different groups on ground of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony) and 353 (making, publishing, or circulating false information, rumors, reports, or alarming news via any medium, including electronic/social media, with the intent to cause fear, alarm, or public disorder, or to incite hatred, enmity, or ill-will between different religious, racial, linguistic, or regional groups) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).The complainant also sought a cyber forensic examination to establish the posts’ authenticity, context and dissemination. articles.title: Ukraine launches nearly 1,200 drones at Russia as peace talks widen to include European security
articles.summary: Ukraine launched nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks since Moscow began its full-scale invasion nearly
articles.body: Ukraine launched nearly 1,200 drones at Russian targets overnight in one of its largest aerial attacks since Moscow began its full-scale invasion nearly five years ago.The strikes came as US and Russian negotiators agreed to discuss wider European security arrangements as part of efforts to end the war, raising concerns among European leaders about the future role of NATO.After two days of talks with Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi this week, US envoys travelled to Moscow to brief Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin. They also met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who was in Dublin, Ireland, for talks with European leaders.US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also President Donald Trump's son-in-law, said further discussions were planned as negotiators sought a breakthrough in the peace efforts.Kushner said Russia had agreed to include European countries in upcoming talks, after Moscow had long opposed their participation, accusing them of supporting Ukraine.The move would allow negotiators "to address the broader postwar European security arrangements alongside the territorial issues between Ukraine and Russia," Kushner said in a post on X.However, European leaders have expressed concern that Moscow could use the discussions to weaken Nato and reshape the continent's security arrangements.They are also wary of US President Donald Trump's praise for Putin and his administration's criticism of European governments.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said Europe did not need to renegotiate its existing security framework. "Russia wants to talk about questions of European security architecture. We don't need to talk about that. There is one," Merz said, referring to Nato, the Associated Press reported.EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said Europe should insist on a ceasefire before moving ahead with further negotiations, a position that differs from Putin's demand."If we start to talk about what Russia is asking regarding the security architecture, we actually walk into the traps that Russia is setting us," she said in Dublin.Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden said European countries must take responsibility for their own future. "We cannot let neither the Americans nor the Russians decide about our future," Frieden said.The Institute for the Study of War said in an assessment on Thursday that Moscow was seeking "to dismantle NATO and the post-Cold War European security architecture".Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia remained open to talks with European governments. "Once we understand (Europe's) true intentions and their readiness to facilitate the peace process, then it will be possible to make a decision on holding a dialogue regarding a settlement in Ukraine in an expanded format," he said.Zelenskyy on Friday renewed his concerns over speed restrictions on the US Starshield system, SpaceX's military-grade version of its Starlink satellite internet service, which Ukraine uses for its defence operations.He said the restrictions were limiting Ukrainian drones to speeds of 161 kph (100 mph) along the front line and in Russian-occupied territories. This, he said, was making it difficult for Ukraine to use interceptor drones against Russia's faster jet-powered drones."We still have no clear explanations," Zelenskyy said, referring to the restrictions, which he had first raised on Thursday.Ukrainian officials are seeking clarification from the US State Department, the Pentagon and SpaceX, he said. Earlier last month, similar restrictions imposed by SpaceX on Ukrainian drone speeds disrupted operations, raising concerns in Kyiv over the impact on US support.SpaceX CEO Elon Musk acknowledged in October that the company had restricted Starlink internet services in Ukraine for about a week. He said the system could not be used for offensive strikes against Russia.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.
